classifier_rationale: The merchant emailed that the return was accepted and a refund issued, but the $79.95 credit has not posted to the card.

retrieved.text: Merchant credit wait period. If the merchant's credit or refund is dated less than 10 business days ago, set the expectation and schedule a follow-up. If it's older, or a statement closed without it, open a billing-error dispute.

Written notice link. After a billing-error intake by phone, send the cardholder a link the same day to submit or confirm the dispute electronically. The cardholder's submission is the written notice under REG-03. The call alone is not. POL-04 does not apply to UN, because notice of unauthorized use can be by phone (REG-12).

What counts as a billing error. A charge the cardholder didn't authorize; a charge that isn't identified properly; goods or services not accepted or not delivered as agreed; a payment or credit not posted properly; a computational error by the issuer; a request for clarification or documentation about a charge; failure to send a statement to the last known address.

note: Cardholder reports returning a blender to KitchenCraft Online for a $79.95 charge dated 2026-09-30. The return was mailed about two weeks before the call. About four business days ago the merchant emailed that the return was accepted and a refund issued. Cardholder has not seen a credit in the app. Cardholder contacted the merchant (return and merchant email). The refund is under 10 business days old, so the POL-03 wait applies: set the expectation and schedule a follow-up. No dispute opened and no notice link sent. Unknown: statement date, exact refund date and amount, and return tracking. If the credit has not posted after the wait period, open a billing-error dispute.
